newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Short Australian debt futures sprint ahead.
newsitem.headline: Short Australian debt futures sprint ahead.

text.p: *Short Australian debt futures rushed ahead as talk of a further easing in monetary policy gripped the market, sending the June bill contract to its highest level since February
Short Australian debt futures rushed ahead as talk of a further easing in monetary policy gripped the market, sending the June bill contract to its highest level since February.

Recent speculation of an easing was fuelled by an article in the Australian Financial Review suggesting that Thursday's downward revision in first quarter wages data left scope for an easing, and possibily before the RBA board meets on June 3.
"It's all on the AFR story. And they suggest it could be as early as today and the market is going with it," said one trader at a European based bank.
The story also knocked back the Australian dollar in offshore trading, practically wiping out Thursday's 1-1/2 cent rally against the U.S. dollar.
The June bill contract extended its SYCOM advance, touching resistance at 94.18 at one stage, which equated to a cash rate of 5.82 percent compared with current 6.0 percent official interest rates.

The revision in first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) took the annual rate to 4.3 percent from an original 4.6 percent and back below the Reserve Bank's 4.5 percent 'line in the sand'.
